speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry whether there is any study conducted to ensure that the liberalisation of the retail electricity market will benefit household consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Following the successful soft launch of the OEM in Jurong, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) commenced the nationwide zonal rollout of the OEM in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The nationwide launch of OEM is progressing well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We observed that more households are choosing to switch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, there is an increasing trend of more households switching.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Households value the choice offered by OEM and are actively choosing the retailer and price plan that best meet their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Households which are looking to switch can benefit from a wide range of competitive offers, incentives and promotions, such as referral programmes, loyalty programmes and bill rebates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Retailers are also offering value-added services and products through tie-ups with third parties, such as banks, telecommunications and home insurance companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Going forward, EMA will continue to work closely with the retailers to roll out the OEM to the remaining zones and actively engage consumers to raise awareness of the OEM and help them make informed choices.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Basically, the new vendors are offering up to 30% discount for the electricity charges.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: What I understand is that there are some concerns about this on the ground, where some segments of the population made a claim that it shows that Singapore Power (SP) Group has been profiteering in the past.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The rationale is that after the 30% discount, the new vendors can still earn an income.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to get the Senior Minister of State's view on this.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, this may change over time, based on market demand and supply, and consumers should be aware that while the price plans offered by retailers are fixed for the duration of each contract, retailers, like all businesses, may adjust their prices and discounts over time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, consumers who have switched to other retailers can also switch back to buy electricity at the regulated tariff from SP Group should they feel that the prices at a different point in time may be more favourable to switch back.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They should check with their retailers if there are any applicable charges when making that decision.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, the key here is to give options to consumers to choose a price plan that best meets their needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think the underlying difference between SP Group and the other retailers is that SP Group has to take into account the long-term cost of infrastructure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: To what extent have these criteria been met thus far and are there any plans to further develop the market to meet these criteria?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in itself, this is a very good outcome from the consumers' perspective.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As this is an early phase in the rollout, we will continue to monitor the take-up rate.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I said before, with each zone of rollout, it seems the increased take-up rate has gone from 11% to 16% to 19%.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, probably, it will stabilise around the 20-something percent level.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But, over time, based on the market fluctuation, as electricity prices fluctuate, perhaps with different bundling as well, the take-up rate may again change.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, this is something that the regulators will watch very closely.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I just want to seek a confirmation from the Minister.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Does this mean that SP Group has been supplying electricity at market rate all this while?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the absence of competition, in the past, when SP Group was the sole monopoly provider, what EMA does is regulate the amount of profit that SP Group can make, and this is benchmarked across electricity providers in other jurisdictions which also operate on the similar structure of a monopoly.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And that is benchmarked across all other jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, with liberalisation by encouraging competition, we allow the market to, therefore, compete based on supply and demand, and bring forth benefits to consumers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But at the end of the day, SP Group will continue to be the provider of last resort.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Should any retailers fail, SP Group will continue to be the one that will provide electricity for all consumers, so that there will be no disruption to the electricity supply.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Given the fact that, in some areas, the switch rates are still rather modest, and there are obviously very large savings to consumers who choose to switch, would the Ministry consider implementing switching on an opt-out basis, perhaps with assignment to a panel of open electricity retailers appointed on, let us say, a competitive tendering basis, because this may allow more consumers to realise the benefits immediately rather than waiting for them to switch?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, this is where the market must play its part.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: EMA, therefore, emphasises a lot on the education of the consumers.
